primary_claim: Measured common image tracks can add decision-relevant information beyond independent reference-source photometric agreement, with a fixed repair-candidate pool.
theory_claim: For a nonempty feasible true-target-depth set, gain-sign identification is equivalent to that set lying on one side of the incumbent-candidate midpoint (strictness stated).
real_scope: 21 historical requests, 105 historical candidates, two exposed scenes; 484 original-valid points and 28 missing requests in fixed 512 population
view_selection: one source pair per scene, largest camera-center separation among six available sources, deterministic lexicographic tie-break; no image or GT scoring
depth_domain: existing PLAN wide bounds; optical reference-camera Z in mm, not inferred from candidate positions

observation.error_budgets: ASSUMED engineering tolerances, not statistical confidence or calibrated true coverage

decision.gain_implementation: Actual frozen 3D coordinates may be off the reference ray. Use affine gain ||a-C-zr||^2-||b-C-zr||^2 over intervals; same-ray midpoint is its special case. It is not NN-to-laser gain.
decision.tie_break: largest worst-case depth squared-error improvement, then smallest candidate id
decision.current_incumbent: the frozen photo_U11 selected coordinate, or original point when its selected_candidate_id is null; outside 21 requests keep frozen photo_U11 output
decision.empty_or_no_guaranteed_gain: KEEP this current photo output, not vacuous acceptance
decision.missing_incumbent: no sign certificate; report separately and keep historical photo output
decision.depth_vs_nn_metrics: separate; midpoint gain does not certify nearest-reference-vertex error

primary_success: cycle common-track selector has lower fixed-population ROI-equal NN MSE than star-only selector and frozen photo selector, with no additional <=1mm to >1mm harms versus frozen photo selector
primary_stage: finite mechanism tests plus fixed-pool old-scene development; cross-scene confirmation deferred until mechanism produces a viable method
do_not_claim: physical layer identity from nearest laser distance
